name: Reverse charge — as defined by the CGST Act
definition: Reverse charge means the liability to pay tax by the recipient of a supply instead of the supplier, under s.9(3) or s.9(4) of the CGST Act or s.5(3) or s.5(4) of the IGST Act. Section 9(3) lets the Government notify categories of supply on which the recipient pays; s.9(4) lets it notify a class of registered persons who pay on specified categories received from an unregistered supplier. In both, all the provisions of the Act apply to the recipient as if he were the person liable to pay the tax. Tax so payable is input tax under s.2(62)(b), so it is capable of being credited on the ordinary conditions.
why_it_exists: Collection is placed where it is enforceable. Where the supplier is outside the net, hard to reach, or numerous and small, the Act moves the payment obligation to the registered recipient, who is already filing.
inputs: the category of the supply and whether it is notified under s.9(3)
the registration status of the supplier
whether the recipient falls in a class notified under s.9(4)
outputs: an output tax liability on the recipient
a corresponding input tax amount, creditable subject to s.16, s.17 and s.18
a self-invoice and a payment voucher, where s.31(3)(f) and (g) apply
preconditions: a supply of goods or services or both has been received
a notification under s.9(3) or s.9(4) covers it
exceptions: the second proviso to s.16(2) does not apply to supplies on which tax is payable on reverse charge basis — see GST-ITC-16-2-P2
s.17(3) requires reverse-charge inward supplies to be included in the value of exempt supply — see GST-ITC-17-3
common_mistakes: treating reverse charge as a rate concession — it moves who pays, not whether tax is due
netting the reverse-charge liability against the credit instead of discharging the liability and then taking credit
applying the one-hundred-and-eighty-day payment rule to a reverse-charge supply, which the proviso excludes
omitting reverse-charge inward supplies from the exempt-supply value in the s.17(2) apportionment
assuming a notification exists — s.9(3) and s.9(4) are enabling provisions; the categories live in notifications, not in the Act
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — a statutory collection mechanism, not an accounting standard question
gst_references: UNKNOWN — which supplies are actually notified under s.9(3) and s.9(4) is not stated in the Act and has not been extracted from a notification here
evidence_required: the category of supply, matched to a notification
the self-invoice under s.31(3)(f) where the supplier is unregistered
confidence_factors: the Act names no supply as reverse-charge; every actual case depends on a notification that is not in this source — any claim about a specific supply is UNKNOWN until that notification is read
weak when the supplier's registration status is unverified
UNKNOWN — source is the Act as updated 31-08-2021; later amendments not held locally
validation_checks: a reverse-charge determination cites a notification, never s.9(3) or s.9(4) alone
the liability is discharged before the corresponding credit is treated as available
a self-invoice exists where the supplier was unregistered
reverse-charge inward supplies appear in the exempt-supply value used for s.17(2)
examples: a registered person receives a supply falling in a category notified under s.9(3); he pays the tax as if he were the supplier, and the tax is input tax under s.2(62)(b)
counterexamples: a registered person buys from an unregistered supplier with no notification under s.9(4) covering that class or category — s.9(4) is enabling only, so no reverse-charge liability arises from the Act itself

section (4) of section 5 of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act;

The Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify categories of supply of goods or services or both, the tax on which shall be paid on reverse charge basis by the recipient of such goods or services or both and all the provisions of this Act shall apply to such recipient as if he is the person liable for paying the tax in relation to the supply of such goods or services or both.

The Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify a class of registered persons who shall, in respect of supply of specified categories of goods or services or both received from an unregistered supplier, pay the tax on reverse charge basis as the recipient of such supply of goods or services or both, and all the provisions of this Act shall apply to such recipient as if he is the person liable for paying the tax in relation to such supply of goods or services or both.
